function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the local working directory. Use for git, tests, installs, and one-off scripts. Do not use it to cat/sed/head/read/write/grep source files — use the read, write, edit, and grep tools instead.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a text file. Returns numbered lines. Use offset (1-based) and limit for large files; if truncated, continue with the next offset. Do not use bash cat/sed/head for this.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return

function.name: write
function.description: Create or overwrite a whole text file. Use for new files or full-file rewrites. Do not use bash cat/heredoc for this. For a small in-place patch, use edit (old must be unique unless replace_all). Path is relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is). content is the full file text; empty string is allowed.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

content.description: Full file text to write. Empty string creates an empty file.

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace a snippet in an existing file. old is exact text (not regex) copied from read without line numbers. old must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true. new may be empty to delete the snippet. Do not use this to create files — use write. Do not use bash sed for this.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

old.description: Exact text to find. Must be unique in the file unless replace_all is true. Cannot be empty.

new.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the snippet.

replace_all.description: If true, replace every occurrence of old. Default false.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with a regex. Returns path:line:content. Optional path (file or directory, default workspace) and glob (e.g. *.py). Prefer this over bash grep. Results are capped; if truncated, narrow path, glob, or pattern. Do not use this to read whole files — use read.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the workspace.

glob.description: Only search files matching this glob, e.g. *.py or *.{ts,tsx}
